SuttaCentral records four translations of the text across four languages [SuttaCentral].
Automated text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus register 71 matching passages shared between the *Saṭṭhikūṭapetavatthu* and three other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Unsurprisingly, the most extensive overlap is with its commentary, the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā*, with 59 matches totaling 5,036 characters (longest correspondence §3.2–8.4 aligned with commentary segment §3178_4–3196 at a similarity score of 0.79) [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares standard verse formulas with other poems in the *Petavatthu*, specifically *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31; 8 matches, with segment §2.1–2.4 displaying a 0.96 similarity to Pv 31 §1.4–2.4) and *Gūthakhādakapetavatthu* (Pv 43; 4 matches, including segment §1.3–4.4 aligned with Pv 43 §1.3–3.4 at 0.83 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus identifies a low-scoring automated cross-language alignment with a Tibetan Kangyur text (BO_K12_D0429_H0405, aligning §13.3 with folio §143b-21–143b-22 with a plausibility score of 20), though this remains a machine alignment rather than a curated textual parallel [DharmaNexus].
